references.text: In the next verse, the conversation continues, and Jesus himself draws near and walks with them as they talk about all that had happened ([ref:Luk 24:15|Luke 24:15]).

Jesus asks what they are discussing, and they explain that it concerns what has happened to Jesus of Nazareth—his suffering, crucifixion, and death ([ref:Luk 24:17-19|Luke 24:17-19]). This expands on the content of the conversation mentioned in verse 14.
The events they discuss include the empty tomb and the angels' message about the resurrection, which were described earlier in the chapter ([ref:Luk 24:1-12|Luke 24:1-12]).

Cleopas and his companion elaborate further on what they discussed: the chief priests' handing over of Jesus, the crucifixion, their disappointed hopes, and the women's report about the empty tomb ([ref:Luk 24:20-24|Luke 24:20-24]).

Mark briefly mentions that Jesus appeared to two of the disciples while they were on their way into the countryside, which likely refers to the same event on the road to Emmaus ([ref:Mark 16:12-13|Mark 16:12-13]).
Malachi describes how those who fear the Lord speak with one another, in a similar way to how these two disciples talked about the Lord's deeds ([ref:Mal 3:16|Malachi 3:16]).
The command to speak of God's words while on the journey is reflected in how the disciples discuss what has happened as they walk ([ref:5 Mos 6:7|Deuteronomy 6:7]).
The first Christians shared everything with each other and talked about what they had experienced, just as these two disciples talk about Jesus' suffering and resurrection ([ref:Apg 4:32|Acts 4:32]).
